title: GC18R Transactional Groundwater Exchange Service Independent Architecture Audit

invariants.note: No alternate SWAP kernel or use-case-specific kernel is introduced.
The exchange contract has no file, format, parser, path or file-unit dependency.
Checkpoint, candidate, prepared handle, result and service responsibilities remain explicitly separated from SWAP physical state and forcing.
Only compact transaction handles cross the seam; no full groundwater state is made persistent per column.
No Newton, Jacobian or constitutive scratch is added to logical columns.
Opaque handles do not prevent pools, SoA storage or batched backend implementations.

Normal prepare-abort-commit sequencing works, but prepared/checkpoint handles are value-copyable and the production contract does not itself enforce or normatively specify one-shot stale-token rejection at the backend boundary. A signature-conforming verifier backend can therefore replay a copied prepared token into irreversible publication. The claimed single-use property is not independently closed.
Abort of a live reservation preserves the committed origin and permits retry; no warm-start restriction is introduced.
The service uses generic finite [t0,t1] coupling windows and no calendar unit.
No midnight, daily duration or fixed coupling-window length is encoded.
Transactional groundwater exchange is represented as runtime/coupler functionality, without claiming downstream orchestration.

The canonical head/flux sign and datum contract is preserved exactly, but unchecked origin_revision+1 at INT64_MAX yields an accepted negative candidate revision, violating valid typed lineage/provenance semantics.

Exact q_GW=-q_SWAP and no mass tolerance remain intact, and prepare/abort normal paths move no committed mass. However irreversible publication is not proven exactly-once for all public-handle usage because copied stale values can reach a backend lacking an explicit mandatory one-shot guard. Absolute mass conservation therefore cannot be certified for admission.
No response-tangent or interface-sensitivity implementation is modified or claimed.
The contract adds no mandatory extra SWAP trajectory or fixed multi-run coupling loop.
No heavy solver/service instance per logical column is required by the API; batching and shared-worker designs remain possible.
No one-to-one MODFLOW-cell to SWAP-column relationship is encoded.
Deep-vadose transfer remains outside SWAP and is not assumed by the service.
No transfer-zone storage is introduced and normal prepare/abort paths publish no physical water.
No specific soil-water solver implementation is assumed.
No crop, ET, drainage, irrigation or surface physics is duplicated or replaced.
No HeadCalc internals, legacy solver arrays or global internals are referenced.
Transaction lifecycle semantics are separate from physical options and numerical solver policy.
No bounded-cost, fallback or throughput claim is introduced; concrete runtime cost remains unqualified.
Reference mode is not modified.
Typed statuses and lifecycle handles support diagnostics before final publication, but replay/overflow defects require explicit remediation diagnostics.
The preparable subtype is opt-in; inactive services need not carry this optional transaction capability.
Participant mapping, concurrency ownership and full system composition remain runtime/coupler responsibilities.
The candidate silently assumes revision headroom for +1 and leaves copied-handle one-shot enforcement to an unstated backend rule. These are hidden dependencies in a transaction/provenance contract.
All 30 invariants were independently reviewed; the result is fail-closed rather than 30-of-30 no-adverse-delta.
